It is not suitable for people who are afraid of getting dirty or tired, have waist and knee problems, or cannot stand the smell of chemicals. This job relies on the body for food, and physical strength and health are the biggest assets.

The common path is: join directly from the position of housekeeper/cleaner → become familiar with the cleaning process and use of chemicals in various places → obtain cleaning-related skill certificates or learn to operate floor scrubbers and high-altitude cleaning equipment → develop into a foreman, project supervisor or management position in a professional cleaning company.

Suitable for people who are quick with their hands and feet, don't mind getting dirty, and are organized. If you can clearly arrange the cleaning order of hundreds of corners in a building, and can endure the loneliness of working silently alone, you are welcome in this industry.

This number is expected to rise to 2,495,500 by 2034, with a net increase of approximately 47,800 jobs, an average annual vacancy of approximately 351,300, and a median annual salary of approximately US$35,900 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace cleaners for very practical reasons: cleaning needs are random, scenarios vary widely, and processing standards are diverse. Robots can currently only handle regular floors. paragraphs: 3/10 shows that the risk of this profession being directly replaced by AI is very low: cleaning needs are highly random, the scenarios are diverse, and robots can only cover regular ground. The focus of the change is the way of operation - equipment shares repetitive work, and people's time shifts to more technical disinfection, management and acceptance.

Low risk does not mean standing still: people who can operate floor scrubbers and disinfection robots, and understand professional cleaning standards and shift management can earn significantly more than ordinary cleaners. The road to pure manual cleaning will become narrower and narrower, and the direction of value-added is to move towards technical positions and management positions.

As a transitional employment, this job has a low threshold and can be entered at any time. It is suitable for short-term savings or family supplementary income. paragraphs: The biggest occupational risk for cleaners is not AI, but the "growth ceiling of low-skilled positions" - there will be more and more equipment, but what determines the upper limit of income is always whether you can upgrade from "sweeping floors" to "knowing equipment, knowing disinfection, and being able to lead a team."

The biggest risk in the job is not AI, but the "mismatch between labor intensity and income": wages are generally not high, and long-term bending, mopping, and contact with cleaning agents cause continuous wear and tear on the waist, knees and respiratory tract; night shifts and temporary fill-in jobs also squeeze life time.
